    SELECT cu.customer_unique_id, COUNT(o.order_id) as order_count
    FROM customers cu
    JOIN orders o ON cu.customer_id = o.customer_id

WITH ranked_orders AS (
  SELECT 
    c.customer_unique_id,
    o.order_purchase_timestamp,
    ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY c.customer_unique_id ORDER BY o.order_purchase_timestamp ASC) as rn
  FROM orders o
  JOIN customers c ON o.customer_id = c.customer_id
),
first_two AS (
  SELECT 
    customer_unique_id,
    MAX(CASE WHEN rn = 1 THEN order_purchase_timestamp END) as first_order,
    MAX(CASE WHEN rn = 2 THEN order_purchase_timestamp END) as second_order
  FROM ranked_orders
  WHERE rn <= 2
  GROUP BY customer_unique_id
  HAVING COUNT(*) >= 2
)
SELECT 
  AVG(julianday(second_order) - julianday(first_order)) as avg_days_between
FROM first_two;
